narrative: While descending through FL240 approximately 45 miles southwest of Boston Logan, flight crew encountered unexpected moderate to severe clear air turbulence. Autopilot momentarily disconnected following a rapid altitude excursion of 800 feet. Crew initiated manual recovery, leveled off at FL230, and coordinated with Boston Center. Seatbelt signs were illuminated prior to encounter; no injuries were reported. Post-flight inspection revealed no structural damage to the airframe.

During initial climb out out of Runway 22R passing 3,500 feet MSL, flight crew observed fluctuating EGT (Exhaust Gas Temperature) and abnormal N1 vibration on engine number 1. Crew executed the uncommanded engine vibration quick reference checklist, reduced power on engine 1, and declared an urgency condition with New York Departure. Radar vectors were provided for an uneventful single-engine overweight landing back on Runway 22L. Airport rescue and firefighting (ARFF) met the aircraft as a standard precaution.

En route at FL340, cabin altitude warning horn sounded with cabin rate of climb indicating 1,500 feet per minute. Flight crew immediately donned oxygen masks and initiated an expedited emergency descent to 10,000 feet in accordance with SOP. Telemetry recorded a rapid descent rate exceeding 4,000 fpm during the initial descent phase. ATC cleared the flight direct to a lower sector. Passenger oxygen masks deployed automatically. The flight diverted safely to Newark without further incident.

While taxiing via Taxiway Bravo toward Runway 04, aircraft crossed the hold short line of Runway 31 without explicit air traffic control clearance. Ground controller observed the conflict and immediately instructed an approaching Cessna Citation on final approach to execute an immediate go-around. Minimum separation was maintained at 1.4 miles. Ground crew reported momentary confusion due to ongoing construction signage and reduced visibility in low dusk lighting.

Shortly after reaching cruise altitude at FL280, primary flight display (PFD) showed an erroneous airspeed disagree and pitot-static mismatch warning. Autothrottle disconnected automatically. Flight crew recognized unreliable airspeed indications, referred to memory items for pitch and power settings, and notified ATC of degraded navigation capabilities. After cross-checking standby instruments, crew confirmed pitot probe heat failure. Flight proceeded to destination at reduced cruise speed without incident.

During descent into Bradley International, ATC instructed flight crew to cross waypoint EXERT at or above 11,000 feet. Due to a late descent clearance in tailwind conditions and FMS vertical navigation path capture lag, the aircraft crossed the fix at 9,800 feet, resulting in a 1,200-foot level bust. Controller issued corrective altitude adjustment to maintain separation with departing traffic. Both crew members acknowledged the vertical deviation and submitted an internal safety report.

During instrument approach to Runway 16 in IMC conditions, flight crew reported dual flight director discrepancy and momentary loss of GPS WAAS signal. Crew aborted the approach at 800 feet AGL and performed a standard missed approach. After resetting the avionics bus and confirming VOR backup reception, the aircraft landed safely via ILS approach.

On initial climb through 8,000 feet, pilots detected an oil pressure drop on engine 2 accompanied by an ECAM warning. Thrust was reduced to flight idle while completing abnormal checklists. Crew decided to return to the departure airport as a precautionary measure. Flight landed uneventfully.
